documents.unit: Southern University System, Office of Academic Affairs
documents.title: Comprehensive Artificial Intelligence Use Policy (SUS-1-004)
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule for all courses: "AI policies fall under faculty discretion" and "faculty have the right to regulate and/or prohibit student use of AI, as they see fit". It lists permitted uses "at faculty discretion", so the decision is handed to instructors; delegates.
documents.summary: A system-wide board-approved policy covering students, faculty and staff. It permits cited AI use in coursework at faculty discretion, bans uncited or unauthorized use as an honor-code violation, restricts faculty and staff use of FERPA data, and sets up advisory councils, appeals and annual review.

units.why: The purpose clause says the policy will "establish a comprehensive framework" for responsible AI use; this is an institution-level preamble, so P56 with phase general and modality informs.
units.anchor: comprehensive framework highlighting the responsible and ethical use of artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: The purpose of this policy is

units.why: The text defines "Artificial Intelligence Systems" as a "machine-based system that generates outputs"; a definition that sets what the policy covers, so P61, informs.
units.anchor: is defined as a machine-based system that generates outputs such as predictions, content

units.why: Defines "Generative AI" with named tools (ChatGPT, Claude AI); definitions of terms that set scope are P61, informs.
units.anchor: AI tools capable of generating text, images, code, or other content

units.why: Defines "Agentic AI" as systems that "act autonomously and make decisions"; a scope definition covering agents, so P61 (P07 is about rules for agents, and this states no rule).
units.anchor: AI systems designed to act autonomously and make decisions on

units.why: Defines "Large Language Model (LLM)" as a model that processes and generates human language; a definition of covered technology, P61, informs.
units.anchor: A type of machine learning model specifically
units.frag_end: based on prompts provided by users.

units.why: The bias definition ends with detection of biases "must be enforced and upheld", an ethics requirement about AI bias; P53 names bias concerns, modality must.
units.anchor: the detection of biases of all kinds
units.fit_note: Frames bias detection as something that must be enforced, not only a concern.

units.why: Software "excluded from the definition of Generative Artificial Intelligence" includes spelling, grammar and plagiarism checks, so these routine features fall outside the rules (unless an instructor says otherwise); P100.
units.anchor: word processing programs and their standard tools (e.g., spelling, grammar, and plagiarism checks)
units.fit_note: Exemption can be overridden if the instructor, supervisor, Vice Chancellor or Chancellor identifies the software otherwise.

units.why: The scope sentence says the policy "applies to all employees, vendors, contractors, and students"; scope setting is P61 and binds everyone.
units.anchor: applies to all employees, vendors, contractors, and students of the Southern

units.why: Community members "are expected to be aware of and comply with this policy"; an expectation to know the institution's guidance. P102 (stay informed) is the nearest; P77 is about law and other policies, not this policy itself.
units.anchor: expected to be aware of and comply with this policy
units.frag_start: All system community members are expected
units.fit_note: Also requires compliance with the policy, not only awareness.

units.why: Failure to comply "may result in non-punitive remedial educational opportunities"; an educative response to misuse, P68 (not P37, no concrete penalty).
units.anchor: non-punitive remedial educational opportunities
units.frag_start: Failure to comply with this policy

units.why: The alternative consequence is "disciplinary actions as outlined in the campus's code of conduct", i.e. integrity or conduct processes handle violations; P36.
units.anchor: disciplinary actions as outlined in the campus’s code of conduct or employment policies
units.frag_start: Failure to comply with this policy
units.fit_note: Covers employee conduct policies too, not only academic misconduct.

units.why: Lists as non-compliance "The misuse of AI to compromise academic integrity", classifying it as a violation; P36.
units.anchor: The misuse of AI to compromise academic integrity.

units.why: Non-compliance includes "Failure to disclose the use of AI"; failing to disclose is itself the violation, so P28.
units.anchor: the use of AI as a tool in assignments

units.why: Non-compliance includes "unauthorized sharing of personally identifiable information (PII) or intellectual property through AI platforms"; data protection, P50 (modality must-not).
units.anchor: unauthorized sharing of personally identifiable information (PII) or intellectual
units.policy: Unauthorized sharing of personally identifiable information (PII) or intellectual property through AI platforms is non-compliance.

units.why: Names "The improper application of AI in hiring or employee evaluations" as non-compliance; consequential decisions about people, P73.
units.anchor: The improper application of AI in hiring or employee evaluations.
units.fit_note: Does not say what makes application improper.

units.why: Outside coursework, "individuals should consult with their supervisor, unit head, Vice Chancellor, or the Chancellor about appropriate use"; this governs non-teaching operations, P76.
units.anchor: individuals should consult with their supervisor, unit head, Vice Chancellor, or the Chancellor

units.why: Within a course, "AI policies fall under faculty discretion": the decision goes to the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: AI policies fall under faculty discretion
units.frag_start: When not explicitly used within a course

units.why: Says "SUS recognizes that AI can be used in appropriate ways that facilitate innovation and creativity" tied to workforce-ready graduates; states benefits rather than a rule, P87.
units.anchor: AI can be used in appropriate ways that facilitate innovation and creativity
units.frag_start: In accordance with SUS’s commitment to academic excellence
units.fit_note: Also links AI to producing graduates ready for the workplace.

units.why: In coursework, AI "as a reference tool, for ideation, research assistance, translation and tutoring purposes is permitted, at faculty discretion"; a list of allowed student uses, nearest P12 (tutoring), which also covers ideation and translation.
units.anchor: reference tool, for ideation, research assistance, translation and tutoring purposes is permitted
units.frag_start: The use of AI as a reference tool
units.fit_note: Lists several uses (reference, ideation, research assistance, translation, tutoring), permitted at faculty discretion and only if acknowledged and cited.

units.why: Permitted use must be "acknowledged and cited in any work submitted"; disclosure with submission, P24.
units.anchor: acknowledged and cited in any work submitted

units.why: Students are "strongly encouraged to check their course syllabi and discuss with their instructor"; students find out each course's rules, P78 (P10 is ask-when-unsure; here the check is general).
units.anchor: strongly encouraged to check their course syllabi and discuss with their instructor
units.frag_end: use of AI in specific courses.

units.why: "Faculty are allowed to use generative AI to enhance teaching materials"; an instructor-use permission for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: Faculty are allowed to use generative AI to enhance teaching materials
units.policy: Faculty are allowed to use generative AI to enhance teaching materials for their respective courses.

units.why: Students "are strictly prohibited from using AI tools to engage in academically dishonest practices", chiefly "submitting work generated by AI as their own without appropriate citation"; P19 (do not have AI produce submitted work).
units.anchor: submitting work generated by AI as their own without appropriate citation
units.fit_note: Ban is on uncited AI-generated work submitted as one's own; cited use is permitted elsewhere.

units.why: "Students who engage in unauthorized or prohibited use of generative AI are subject to the University's academic honor code"; misuse handled as academic honor code violation, P36.
units.anchor: subject to the University’s academic honor code

units.why: "By default, students will violate the academic honor code if they use AI without citation (as this constitutes plagiarism)"; uncited use is a violation, P28.
units.anchor: if they use AI without citation (as this constitutes plagiarism)

units.why: The same sentence adds a violation if students use AI "without instructor permission": when permission is absent, AI use is out, which is a fallback rule, P06.
units.anchor: or without instructor permission.

units.why: Students "will also violate academic integrity if they fail to verify that AI has provided correct and factual information"; students must verify output, P31.
units.anchor: fail to verify that AI has provided correct and factual information

units.why: Students doing AI research "should collaborate with their faculty advisor ... and should document methodology, data sources, and algorithms"; research use, P62.
units.anchor: should collaborate with their faculty advisor or relevant supervisor
units.fit_note: Is about research that involves AI and requires documenting methodology, data sources and algorithms.

units.why: Faculty who use AI "should ensure that any parameters for use are clearly stated in the course syllabus, announcements, and assignment instructions"; P09.
units.anchor: parameters for use are clearly stated in the course syllabus, announcements, and assignment instructions
units.fit_note: Applies to faculty who elect to incorporate AI, not all faculty.

units.why: Faculty "should be aware and inform students that data entered into AI software may become part of the software's training"; privacy warning to students, P50.
units.anchor: data entered into AI software may become part of the software’s training
units.frag_start: Faculty should be aware and inform
units.fit_note: Instructors are to tell students; the rule is a warning about training use, not a vetted-tool preference.

units.why: "Faculty determine what constitutes misuse of AI as a tool for coursework in their courses"; per-instructor decision, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty determine what constitutes misuse of AI as a tool for coursework

units.why: "faculty have the right to regulate and/or prohibit student use of AI, as they see fit, from particular and/or all coursework"; instructors set the rule, P04.
units.anchor: faculty have the right to regulate and/or prohibit student use of AI

units.why: Faculty who prohibit AI "could revise assignments that lend themselves to easily using AI generated content"; assignment redesign, P35 (modality may, as it is a suggestion).
units.anchor: could revise assignments that lend themselves to easily using AI generated content
units.frag_start: Faculty prohibiting the use of AI

units.why: "Faculty are not permitted to use generative AI to produce course materials without proper attribution"; AI-made course materials must be disclosed, P48.
units.anchor: not permitted to use generative AI to produce course materials without proper attribution
units.frag_start: Faculty are not permitted to use
units.fit_note: Requires attribution; does not mention instructor review of the materials.

units.why: Faculty "are also prohibited from uploading or sharing any student information covered under FERPA with an AI system"; protecting student data, P50.
units.anchor: prohibited from uploading or sharing any student information covered under FERPA with an AI system

units.why: "Policy violations will be noted during annual evaluations, and corrective action(s) with a focus on educational remedies will be taken"; consequences for faculty are routed through performance evaluation; no type covers employee accountability.
units.anchor: Policy violations will be noted during annual evaluations
units.uncovered_note: Faculty violations of the AI policy are recorded in annual evaluations and met with corrective action focused on educational remedies.

units.why: Staff "are not permitted to use generative AI to produce materials used in their area of work without proper attribution"; attribution for AI-made materials, P48 (staff, not course materials).
units.anchor: not permitted to use generative AI to produce materials used in their area of work
units.frag_start: Staff are not permitted to use
units.fit_note: About staff work materials generally, not course materials, and mentions no review.

units.why: "Staff are prohibited from uploading or sharing any student information covered under FERPA with an AI system"; P50.
units.anchor: prohibited from uploading or sharing any student information
units.frag_start: Staff are prohibited from uploading or

units.why: Staff violations "will be noted during annual evaluations, and corrective action(s)... taken as warranted"; same employee-accountability pattern as for faculty, no fitting type.
units.anchor: Policy violations will be noted during annual evaluations, and corrective
units.uncovered_note: Staff violations of the AI policy are recorded in annual evaluations and met with corrective action as warranted.

units.why: AI detection tools "are imperfect and may produce false positives, may be biased against non-native speakers"; detectors are unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools presently available are imperfect and may produce false positives
units.frag_end: keep up with rapidly changing AI.

units.why: Says "Establishing clear expectations, communicating those expectations, building relationships ... and designing authentic assessments" will create an unbiased environment; assessment design advice, nearest P35.
units.anchor: designing authentic assessments will be impactful ways to create an
units.frag_start: Establishing clear expectations, communicating those expectations
units.fit_note: Combines clear expectations, relationship-building and authentic assessment as alternatives to detection.

units.why: If detection tools suggest AI use, "that should be the start of data gathering and not the end decision making tool"; detector output is not proof, P69.
units.anchor: should be the start of data gathering and not the end decision making tool
units.frag_start: If AI detection tools are used

units.why: Lists evidence to gather: "obvious mistakes", "references that are made-up", writing "not in keeping with past writing"; kinds of evidence to weigh, P69.
units.anchor: references that are made -up or not actually relevant to the content
units.frag_start: Data gathering could include: obvious mistakes

units.why: "A conversation with the person suspected of improperly using AI should take place when additional evidence is presented"; talk to the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: A conversation with the person suspected of improperly using AI should take place
units.frag_start: A conversation with the person suspected

units.why: Faculty who suspect violation "should follow the procedures under the Student's Code of Conduct policy"; formal procedure, P81.
units.anchor: should follow the procedures under the Student’s Code of Conduct policy

units.why: "Ensure our System's AI governance framework aligns with national and state AI policies"; alignment with external law and policy, P77.
units.anchor: AI governance framework aligns with national and state AI policies

units.why: "Each campus may form an Advisory Council to assist with the development and implementation of AI-related policies, training, workshops and/or curricula"; names a body that maintains the policy, P80.
units.anchor: Each campus may form an “Advisory Council” to assist with the development
units.fit_note: Council is optional and advisory rather than a body that enforces.

units.why: The Council may "Review AI decision-making tools in admissions, grading, hiring, and research to prevent bias"; monitoring deployed AI systems for bias, P98.
units.anchor: Review AI decision -making tools in admissions, grading, hiring, and research to prevent bias
units.frag_start: Ethical and Fair Use Monitoring: Review
units.fit_note: Review of decision tools for bias; no mention of documentation.

units.why: The Council may "Leverage AI to support early alert systems, academic advising, and student retention strategies"; AI in student services, P76.
units.anchor: Leverage AI to support early alert systems, academic advising, and student retention strategies
units.frag_start: AI in Student Success Initiatives: Leverage

units.why: The Council may "Partner with industry leaders and policymakers to create internship and career opportunities in AI fields"; partnerships, P88.
units.anchor: Partner with industry leaders and policymakers to create internship and career opportunities

units.why: "Workshops and resources on responsible AI use will be provided for faculty, staff, and students"; training offered to students and staff too, P70.
units.anchor: Workshops and resources on responsible AI use will be provided for faculty, staff, and students

units.why: "Each campus, especially academic units, will develop clear AI usage guidelines in their syllabi"; syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: will develop clear AI usage guidelines in their syllabi

units.why: "Students must obtain prior approval from the instructor before recording any lectures"; AI-policy section rule on recording, P86 (consent before recording), though AI is not named.
units.anchor: Students must obtain prior approval from the instructor before recording any lectures

units.why: "Procedures for identifying and addressing AI misuse will be established and communicated"; a commitment to create procedures, nearest P81.
units.anchor: Procedures for identifying and addressing AI misuse will be established and communicated.

units.why: "Students accused of AI misuse will have access to a transparent appeal process"; right to respond, P64.
units.anchor: Students accused of AI misuse will have access to a transparent appeal process

units.why: "An Advisory Council will review the policy annually"; a review cycle, P54.

units.anchor: This policy aligns with the following laws, regulations, and guidelines

units.why: Calls itself "a new policy developed to address the evolving role of artificial intelligence" that "will become effective upon approval by the System Board Chair and President"; how the policy was adopted, P84.
units.anchor: will become effective upon approval by the System Board Chair and President
units.frag_start: This is a new policy developed

units.why: The policy "will be reviewed annually" with interim reviews "as needed"; review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: It will be reviewed annually to ensure alignment with advancements in AI technology

units.why: "the SU System Policy and Planning Committee shall electronically post and archive approved and signed system policies"; names who maintains the policy, P80.
units.anchor: SU System Policy and Planning Committee shall electronically post and archive approved
units.fit_note: Covers posting and archiving, not interpretation or enforcement.

units.why: The header names "Responsible Units: System Office of Academic Affairs" and the Vice President, Academic Affairs; owner of the policy, P80.
units.anchor: Responsible Units: System Office of Academic Affairs

documents.title: Recent Policy Approval Briefs: Comprehensive AI Use Policy (SUS-6-001)
documents.stance_why: The brief gives a summary ("establishes a university-wide framework") and a general aim of "prohibiting misuse of AI technologies" but states no rule on student use in courses, so no allow or ban is set; delegates is the closest fit.
documents.summary: A short public brief on the campus policy page summarizing the AI use policy. It states a framework, an AI Advisory Council and compliance aims but sets no rules for course-level AI use. Only the AI entry is coded; the other policies listed are unrelated.

units.why: The brief says the university "establishes a university-wide framework for the ethical, responsible, and compliant use of Artificial Intelligence"; institution-wide framework, P56.
units.anchor: establishes a university-wide framework for the ethical, responsible, and compliant use
units.frag_start: Southern University and A&M College establishes

units.why: The brief says it "establishes institutional oversight through an AI Advisory Council"; a body named to oversee the policy, P80.
units.anchor: establishes institutional oversight through an AI Advisory Council
units.frag_start: The policy defines acceptable AI use,

units.why: The brief says it "ensures compliance with academic integrity, privacy, and security standards"; compliance with existing standards, P77.
units.anchor: ensures compliance with academic integrity, privacy, and security standards

units.why: The policy statement says the university will govern AI "while prohibiting misuse of AI technologies"; a general prohibition on misuse that does not say what misuse is, so no type fits.
units.anchor: while prohibiting misuse of AI technologies
units.frag_start: Southern University and A&M College will govern
units.uncovered_note: A general statement that the university prohibits misuse of AI technologies, without defining misuse.

units.why: The statement commits to "oversight mechanisms that promote transparency, accountability, academic integrity, privacy protection, and responsible innovation"; principles statement, P56.
units.anchor: promote transparency, accountability, academic integrity, privacy protection, and responsible innovation
units.frag_start: Southern University and A&M College will govern

notes: Coder B. Only the two included university-layer documents coded. Definitions of Narrow, Reactive, Limited Memory, Theory of Mind, AGI, Deep Learning, Data Science, ML, NLP and PII were not coded as separate units (technical glossary). The brief's policy number (SUS-6-001) and dates differ from the full text (SUS-1-004). Full text comes from a third-party Drive link.
